text:
incident-bot: PAGER: High GPU request queue and autoscale failures in eu-west-1. Severity: Sev2. Notifying infra-oncall and runtime teams.

ashley: oncall here. Grafana shows inference-pool-eu-west queue growth to ~12k requests, 95th token latency jumped to ~2.4s. Autoscaler logs: repeatedly attempted to scale, but new nodes fail readiness checks and we hit max-replicas.

callie: thanks. Runtime/driver team, can you check node kernel logs for Xid or OOMs? Any sign of driver-level faults?

jorge: looking now. Multiple nodes report GPU errors: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 13" in dmesg and container logs show `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS`. Also saw several ml-infer processes terminated by OOM.

sam: that Xid 13 pattern aligns with recent driver/kernel mismatches. Any driver/kernel rollouts in eu-west in last hour?

ashley: we deployed a driver/kernel update to the eu-west reserved pool ~35 minutes ago to address a perf regression. Autoscaler began provisioning nodes with the new image ~30 minutes ago.

callie: customer impact: a subset of high-throughput customers on hosted are seeing increased 5xxs and rate-limited throughput. Support, please notify affected accounts and post a public incident note.

mike: already sent initial messages to top impacted customers ~8 minutes ago. They're asking for ETA and whether we have mitigation steps.

jorge: I reproduced the fault on a test node with the new driver under heavy KV cache and batching: device memory corruption followed by Xid 13. Rolling back driver on that test node clears the errors.

ashley: immediate mitigation plan proposal: (1) freeze autoscaler so it stops creating nodes with the new image, (2) cordon + drain nodes running the new driver variant, (3) spin up replacement nodes from the last-stable snapshot, (4) temporarily lower hosted-tier burst limits to shrink queue growth. Open to feedback.

sam: +1. I'll flip the autoscaler to emergency-freeze and enable priority provisioning for the stable snapshot. Also will monitor node provisioning TTL.

callie: additional mitigation: route traffic for heavy models to smaller-quantized variants (model-fallback) to reduce device memory pressure. I'll update routing rules now.

ashley: cordon/drain started for 6 affected nodes. Using graceful drain with 60s max-term to minimize in-flight failures. Replacement nodes from snapshot-stable-20260210 are booting.

jorge: preparing a runtime-level config tweak: reduce batch size and prefetch settings via configmap for live pods to lower memory churn while replacements come online. Also building a driver handshake hotfix, but that will take ~2-3 hours to validate and stage. Rollback is much quicker.

mike: customer comms update sent: "We are redirecting traffic to stable nodes and limiting non-essential throughput. Expected user impact to diminish within ~30-45 minutes as replacements finish booting. Engineering investigating root cause; full patch ETA a few hours. Will update every 30 minutes or on major changes."

incident-bot: NOTE: On-call handoff scheduled in 15 minutes (ashley -> callie). Use `/hand-off` to record.

ashley: handoff note -> callie: autoscaler is frozen, 3/6 replacement nodes up, rolling rollback in progress. Key metrics to watch: queue depth, 95th token latency, and frequency of Xid events in kernel logs. Please own customer updates after takeover.

callie: taking ownership. I'll continue customer comms and coordinate rollback vs hotfix with runtime. Jorge, recommend prioritized rollback to stable image across the pool, then hold hotfix to a canary until we get baseline.

jorge: starting automated rollback across nodes with the affected label. Also applying the batch-size throttle. After initial rollbacks, Xid counts dropped to zero on rolled nodes. Continuing rollout and monitoring.

sam: autoscaler freeze confirmed. Replacement nodes booting: now 4/6. Metrics: queue 12k -> 6.8k, 95th token latency 2.4s -> 1.6s. Pod restart rate decreasing on drained nodes, still seeing restarts on any remaining patched nodes.

callie: posted public incident update and flagged for follow-up evaluation on model-fallback quality. Support looped in on customer replies.

jorge: will hold hotfix until a stable baseline is observed; plan to test hotfix on a small canary pool once everything is stable.

ashley: keeping incident open until queue < 500 and error-rate back to baseline. Next update in 15 minutes or on major change. :thumbsup:
